messages.subject: unsolicited opinions about your pricing page
messages.body:
You didn't ask for this and you can ignore all of it.

I was showing someone Thicket as an example of a good vertical wedge and ended up staring at your pricing page for twenty minutes. Three things:

Your per-seat pricing is fighting your own product. A two-vet clinic has eleven people who touch the schedule and two people who generate revenue. Per-seat means the front desk is a cost, so they'll share a login, and then your usage data is garbage and you won't know it for a year.

The $180 tier has no name. The other two do. It reads like the one you don't want anyone to pick, which is presumably not true since it's the one most clinics should be on.

And you're apologizing for the price in the FAQ. "We know practice management software is expensive" — they know. Every one of them is paying more than that today for something worse.

Separately, and unrelatedly: do you want an intro to Corbin Achebe? He ran ops for a twelve-clinic group in Portland before he went independent and he is the single most useful person I know on how clinics actually buy. He'll take the call if I ask.

J

messages.subject: Re: unsolicited opinions about your pricing page
messages.body:
The per-seat thing is correct and slightly ruinous to read at 11pm.

We went per-seat because it was the thing I understood how to build, which is a bad reason that I have been calling a pricing strategy for four months. You're right that they'll share a login. Ros's clinic almost certainly already does and I've never once looked.

The FAQ line is going. That's just fear written down.

I'm less sure about naming the middle tier. Part of me thinks an unnamed tier reads as the boring default and the boring default is where you want most people to land. But I think you're right that it currently reads as the one we're embarrassed by, which is a different thing.

And yes to Corbin, genuinely. That's exactly the person I don't have.

Best,
Priya

messages.subject: Re: unsolicited opinions about your pricing page
messages.body:
Done, intro going out this morning. I told him you'd ask better questions than the last three founders he talked to, so no pressure.

On the middle tier, fair pushback. Boring default is a real strategy. I'd just make sure it's boring on purpose and not boring because nobody got to it.

J
